thread:
Maya: Heads up — SEA POP p99 shot up ~10:12 UTC, throughput dropped ~18%. Clients reporting timeouts. Seeing kernel autoselect churn + long queueing in the batcher.
Sam: Copy, can you paste the runtime selector log and /metrics snapshot?
Maya: Pasted a short excerpt:```
[10:11:58] selector: picked fp16_large_seq_kernel for model-x seq=1024 latency_est=45ms
[10:11:59] selector: fallback fp16_small_seq_kernel due to OOM margin low
[10:12:00] selector: picked fp16_large_seq_kernel for same shard -> schedule bump
[10:12:02] batcher: queue_len=42 avg_wait=78ms inflight=8
```
Noah: infra-bot shows no deploys in the window (noah:infra-bot:deploys OK). Network metrics show TCP retransmits spike for SEA->peer ranges at 10:11:~10:14.
Raj: Checked upstream BGP logs — our peer in SEA had an unscheduled path change at 10:10:50 (AS Path changed, routing via different exchange). Likely asymmetric path + increased RTT.
Leah: If RTT increases, kernel selector's latency model can oscillate — it tries larger kernels to amortize throughput but the added RTT pushes it over SLO and forces fallback, causing churn.
Sam: Can you share tcp stats? small snippet helps (tcpdump / netstat -s).
Maya: tcpdump 1s sample:```
10:12:01.234 IP 10.0.5.23 > 44.33.12.7: Flags [P.], seq 12345:12400, ack 9876, win 5120, length 55
10:12:01.240 IP 44.33.12.7 > 10.0.5.23: Flags [R], seq 2222, ack 3333, win 0, length 0
--- summary --- retransmits: 3 pkts/sec, dup_ack: twice, MSS seen 1460, some segs show DF set + ICMP frag-needed from core-router
```
Noah: ICMP frag-needed + MTU mismatch on path -> likely middlebox or peering link dropping large packets. We build with large frame sizes (GSO) which can amplify.
Raj: Confirmed with provider: they had a peering reroute to an alternate IX with different MTU handling at 10:10:40 while doing maintenance. They rolled back at 10:17 UTC but we saw residual packet reassembly issues.
Maya: Runtime profile for the same interval shows kernel hot path switching:```
10:11:55 cpu: kernel_selector::score(fp16_large_seq) = 0.82
10:11:56 cpu: kernel_selector::score(fp16_small_seq) = 0.34
10:12:00 cpu: selector fell back -> cache invalidation -> kvcache.misses +15%
10:12:03 perf: batch_wait_ratio +0.21 -> backpressure on serve threads
```
Leah: So two things compounding: network MTU/transmit issues causing retransmits/extra RTT; selector reacts to increased observed latency and switches kernels, causing KV cache eviction patterns and batcher queue growth. Noisy neighbor effect from bigger frames increases wait.
Sam: Short mitigation steps we can do immediately: 1) Force runtime to pin smaller kernel family in SEA pop (override selector to prefer small_seq when RTT > 20ms) 2) Cap max batch size to 16 for the pop to reduce packet sizes 3) Temporarily enable prefix KV pinning for hot routes to avoid eviction thrash.
Maya: I'll flip a runtime config (will do gradual config change via console canary -> full). Plan: set kernel_override=fp16_small_seq_kernel for model-x, set batch_max=16, set kvcache.reserved=0.12. Rolling to canary now.
infra-bot: change_requested "runtime-config" by Maya queued at 10:13:50, canary targeting 1/10 hosts in SEA pop.
Sam: Monitor p95/p99 and kvcache misses. Also watch token-cost impact (smaller kernels higher CPU per token).
Noah: Also filed provider ticket #SEA-PEER-312 with carrier. They acknowledged and will re-evaluate peering config.
Leah: Postmortem actions to add: - make selector aware of network RTT variance (decouple kernel score from single-sample latency) - add automatic batch-size cap when retransmit rate > threshold - Add MTU probe checks as part of POP health (periodic traceroutes + MTU checks)
Maya: Canary applied: first 1 host shows p99 down from 230ms -> 95ms, queue_len down to 10, kvcache.misses down 9%. Scaling to 3 hosts now.
Sam: Good. Can we make a short rollback plan if cpu goes too high? Maya: yes — rollback knob is kernel_override=null and batch_max=32; will execute if CPU > 85% for sustained 30s.
Leah: Adding follow-ups to infra board (sre-ops): write selector unit test to simulate RTT jitter, add e2e for batcher backpressure.
Maya: Will keep thread updated. If carrier confirms fix we'll slowly relax overrides. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Noah: Thanks — keeping an eye on provider ticket and net metrics.
infra-bot: incident: provider-peering -> SEA POP elevated retransmits resolved at 10:17:20 per provider note
Maya: Post-fix numbers: p99 stabilized ~80-90ms, throughput returned to normal after overrides relaxed at 10:35. Will open a perf regression issue to track selector behavior across similar network anomalies.
Leah: Filed PERF-1289 with suggested mitigations and spec for network-aware selector. Assigning to eng-runtime team.
Sam: Nice work triaging quickly. Short doc later describing the kernel-selection heuristics and network interplay would help oncall.
Maya: Agreed — I'll draft a short runbook snippet and link to this thread.
